subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept requester-owned outbound-only `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` as the public A2A authorization contract, or require target-side receive/per-capability policy before landing this PR?
rationale: The PR changes cross-agent session authorization and adds a public config/SDK surface, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term security boundary or product contract.

options.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
options.body: Accept requester-owned outbound semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, branch refresh, and focused validation before merge.

options.title: Require broader authorization first
options.body: Pause this branch and fold the work into bidirectional or per-capability session authorization before exposing a new config contract.

options.title: Keep as experimental discussion
options.body: Leave the PR open for design discussion but do not land the public config surface until the broader per-agent scoping issue is resolved.

recommendation.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
recommendation.body: Accept requester-owned outbound semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, branch refresh, and focused validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on session allowlist hardening, plugin SDK boundaries, and config policy surfaces touched by this PR.
